_note: Headline findings of the CAG Performance Audit of the Delhi Jal Board, extracted verbatim-faithfully from the CAG's own press release (24 March 2026, ref BSC/SS/RK/IK/15-26). The press release is the government-stamped summary; chapter/page-level citations from the full report PDF (seven chapters) can be added when individual facts need deeper anchoring. Extraction 2026-07-20; figures are the audit period FY2017-18 to FY2021-22 unless dated otherwise.

report.title: Performance Audit of 'Functioning of Delhi Jal Board'
report.auditor: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
report.tabled_in: Legislature of the NCT of Delhi

findings.stat: Raw-water shortage against assessed requirement rose from 22% (2017-18) to 24% (2021-22); potable-water shortage rose from 24.2% to 25.79%
No flow meters at WTPs, reservoirs, water emergencies and borewells - the quantity of water treated, extracted, transmitted or supplied could not be measured accurately
Water testing was not being done as per BIS norms
Transmission loss of water increased from 16% to 21% during 2017-22
Per-capita potable availability was below 20 GPCD in four zones and below 40 GPCD in eight zones, against the 60 GPCD requirement
Non-Revenue Water ran at 51-53% of average daily supply, affecting revenues to the tune of Rs 4,988 crore
Of 594 MGD sewage generated, 545 MGD was treated by 35 STPs
212.59 MGD of sewage from 1,080 unauthorised colonies was dumped untreated into storm-water drains
Treated effluent released by 25 STPs into the Yamuna did not meet DPCC norms; no mechanism existed to monitor faecal coliform in treated effluent

Planning failures delayed the Chandrawal WTP rehabilitation and led the Asian Development Bank to withdraw Rs 2,243 crore of financing for the Wazirabad WTP rehabilitation under the Delhi Water Supply Improvement Investment Programme
Total outstanding loan of DJB with interest stood at Rs 66,595 crore (March 2022)
Accounts were submitted for statutory audit only up to 2021-22, and Separate Audit Reports opined they do not depict 'a true and fair picture' of DJB's affairs
In 2021-22 DJB billed only 371 MGD (40%) of the potable water it produced; of that, only 244 MGD (66%) was billed on meter readings
Shortfalls in revenue receipts against budget ranged between 11.28% and 41.71%
Shortage of regular staff increased continuously from 23.09% to 32.12% over the audit period; a 3,057-staff mismatch existed between the salary system (IFMS) and wing-level records

recommendations_summary: Formulate a water policy and perspective plan matched to Delhi's population growth
Install regularly calibrated flow meters at all WTP/UGR/tube-well inlet and outlet points and conduct a water audit
Improve quality-testing laboratories to test against all prescribed parameters
Prescribe a maintenance and upgradation schedule for water and sewerage infrastructure, including GPS trackers on water tankers
Expedite collection of outstanding dues with emphasis on large and institutional consumers
Address the serious shortage of staff immediately
